cohort: The study recruited 200 neonates presenting with skin lesions at a tertiary care teaching hospital.
finding: The study identified Erythema toxicum neonatorum, sebaceous gland hyperplasia, and Mongolian Spots as the most prevalent neonatal dermatoses, with various associations found between specific dermatoses and perinatal risk factors.
mod_finding: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum and salmon patch were significantly higher in vaginally delivered neonates, while Mongolian Spots and Superficial Desquamation were significantly higher in neonates born by C-section.
cross-section timing: During the neonatal period, at presentation with skin lesions.
birth_weight: Various, including <1.5 kg, 2.6-3.5 kg (majority), and >3.5 kg.
gest_age: Full term (majority) and post term neonates.
